standard_prerequisites.name: Invertible modules are finite locally free of rank one and their duals are inverse
standard_prerequisites.use: Justifies that L is finite locally free and that varphi(L) is an invertible ideal, which is what makes the localization argument available.

standard_prerequisites.name: Uniqueness of prime factorization in a UFD and its preservation under localization
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the arithmetic input that forces b_j = c_j in the final comparison.

standard_prerequisites.name: The cover criterion for an ideal to be generated by a given element
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces generating I by h to the case where I_a is principal for a single a.

core_obligations: For an invertible module L, use that L is finite locally free, hence torsion free and finite over R, and choose a nonzero varphi in Hom_R(L, R) so that I = varphi(L) is an invertible ideal of R (proof lines 36189-36193).
Choose a nonzero f in I and write its prime factorization f = u p_1^{e_1} ... p_r^{e_r} with the p_i pairwise distinct (proof lines 36194-36198).

Use finite local freeness of L to find a_i not in (p_i) with I_{a_i} = (g_i), note p_i is still prime in the UFD R_{a_i}, write g_i = p_i^{c_i} g'_i with g'_i not divisible by p_i, and conclude e_i >= c_i (proof lines 36199-36203).
Claim that I is generated by h = p_1^{c_1} ... p_r^{c_r} (proof line 36204).

Prove the claim by the cover criterion: for any a with I_a = (g) principal, let J be the set of i with p_i a nonunit in R_a, use f in I_a to write g = v prod_{i in J} p_j^{b_j} with v a unit and b_j <= e_j (proof lines 36208-36215).

For each j in J use I_{a a_j} = g R_{a a_j} = g_j R_{a a_j} to conclude that g and g_j become associates in R_{a a_j}, so that uniqueness of factorization in the UFD R_{a a_j} gives b_j = c_j, completing the proof (proof lines 36216-36218).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that Pic(R) is trivial for a UFD (source lines 36183-36186). The proof is a genuine argument with a reduction and a prime-factorization comparison. It takes an invertible module L, uses that L is finite locally free hence torsion free and finite, and picks a nonzero element varphi of the dual so that I = varphi(L) is an invertible ideal of R (proof lines 36189-36193). Factoring a nonzero f in I as u p_1^{e_1} ... p_r^{e_r} into pairwise distinct primes, it then uses finite local freeness of L to find a_i not in (p_i) with I_{a_i} = (g_i), writes g_i = p_i^{c_i} g'_i with g'_i not divisible by p_i, and reads off e_i >= c_i (proof lines 36194-36203). The claim that I is generated by h = p_1^{c_1} ... p_r^{c_r} is then verified by the cover criterion: for any a with I_a principal, say I_a = (g), the set J of indices whose primes become nonunits in R_a is analysed, the prime factorizations of g and f are compared to get b_j <= e_j, and the compatibility I_{a a_j} = g R_{a a_j} = g_j R_{a a_j} together with uniqueness of factorization forces b_j = c_j (proof lines 36208-36218). The non-routine content is the two-level comparison of the same ideal after two different localizations.
